$comment: Stage 7 adjacent-page prefetch contract. The window is measured in SPREADS, not pages, because a double-page spread is the unit the reader can actually be sitting on. Shared by Rust (komga_core::reader::prefetch) and Swift (KomgaReader.Prefetch).

rules.window: center spread index, forward F spreads ahead, back B spreads behind. F/B/cap are NOT chosen here: since Stage 8 they are computed per reading session by reader/window.json from device memory, page size, network and motion. The F/B/cap values in these cases are therefore inputs to the queueing rule, not recommendations, and the `defaults` block is only the fallback used when a caller supplies no device profile at all.
rules.order: Deterministic and asserted exactly: (1) the center spread's pages in reading order, (2) +1..+F spreads ahead, pages in reading order, (3) -1..-B spreads behind, pages in reading order. Center first so the visible page is never queued behind a neighbor.
rules.skipCached: Pages already present in the page cache are dropped from the queue, but they still occupy their window slot (a cached neighbor does not pull a farther neighbor into the window).
rules.dropped: The set of cached pages that fell inside the window, reported ascending and de-duplicated, independent of `cap`. It is diagnostics for the cache-hit ratio, not a fetch order.
rules.clamp: Spread indices outside [0, spreadCount) are dropped. The center itself is clamped into range first, so an out-of-range center can never produce an empty queue for a non-empty book.
rules.cap: After ordering and skipping, the queue is truncated to at most `cap` entries, dropping from the TAIL (the least useful = furthest behind).
rules.supersede: When the center moves, everything in the previous queue that is not in the new queue and not already in flight is cancelled. In-flight downloads finish rather than being torn down mid-byte — a partial file is worse than a wasted one, and the cache accounting treats a file as a miss unless it is complete.
rules.neverBlocksRender: Prefetch is advisory: a queue item that fails must not surface an error for the visible page, and the visible page is loaded through the same pipeline with its own request.

cases.name: fast-flip-supersedes-the-old-window
cases.$comment: The reader jumps from spread 2 to spread 19. Page 4 was already downloading when the flip happened, so it is left in flight instead of being cancelled mid-byte. `spreads: null` plus `spreadCount` means that many one-page spreads.
